newsitem.title: EGYPT: 20 missing from tourist boat mishap on Nile.
newsitem.headline: 20 missing from tourist boat mishap on Nile.

text.p: Twenty people aboard a Nile cruiser were feared drowned when the boat took on water and listed in a storm in southern Egypt, the Interior Ministry said on Friday.
It said the missing were nine Czech and five Slovak tourists and six Egyptian crew members.
More than 100 other people on the cruiser Amira Jihan survived.
Rescue work resumed at dawn and a ministry spokesman said: "They are trying to float the boat and get out anyone who is stuck inside," a ministry spokesman said.
Czech consul Vratislav Janda told Reuters: "The missing people are from the cabins that are under the water.
"Two of the survivors are badly injured, one with a broken leg."

The ministry spokesman blamed strong winds and strong currents for the accident, which happened on Thursday afternoon near the village of al-Mufalsa, about 580 km (360 miles) south of the capital Cairo.
He said the Amira Jihan was carrying 77 Czechs and Slovaks and 51 Egyptian crew members. Sixty-three of the tourists and 45 of the crew had escaped.

In the early hours of Friday, an official in Edfu, the nearest large town, said: "We have rescued 63 tourists and brought them to Edfu. Local people went out in small boats and pulled some of them out through the windows but they can't work now because it is pitch dark."
The survivors spent the night in Edfu hospital, some of them with injuries, and Janda said most of them moved on Friday morning to a hotel in the resort of Luxor.
"Of course they left the boat with just the clothes they were wearing. They don't have passports or any of their possessions," he added.
A policeman in Aswan, the provincial capital, said: "We think that while the captain was trying to dock the boat along the shore, the boat tipped over because of the strong wind."

In the last major accident on the Nile, dozens of people drowned in September when an overloaded ferry capsized while bringing them home from a funeral. That accident took place further north, in the province of Minya.
